To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the data decomposition of an algorithm can have a significant effect on its performance on parallel computers, (2) the data decomposition can be changed at runtime without affecting the correctness of the program, and (3) the data decomposition is not a fixed property of a program, but rather a property that depends on the program's environment, which can include the number of processors, their memory sizes, and the topology of their interconnection network.

the use of derivative functions and of a configuration parameter to describe the data decomposition can make programs with explicit communication easier to write, more efficient to execute, and more portable to different machines.
